name: AIDev v3 agent lane study
frozen: 2026-10-24, before any landed clean outcome or score was computed
fix_message_notes: The spec says a fixing commit's message starts with fix, Fix, revert or Revert; matched case-insensitively at the start with no word boundary, so 'fixes' and 'fixed' count. A reference to the pull request's own number (#n) also counts. The pull request's own commits and its merge commit are excluded.
leakage_notes: Claude Haiku 4.5 training data cutoff Jul 2025, reliable knowledge cutoff Feb 2025, from https://platform.claude.com/docs/de/models/haiku-4-5/overview (read 24 October 2026). Every ticket in the sample was created before 2 June 2025, so the leakage subset is empty; the check is reported as not runnable on this dataset.

Copilot.notes: Opens pull requests and commits from its own account Copilot (18,882 of 23,813 commits). A commit by any other account that is not a bot and not a merge from the base branch is a human commit.

Devin.notes: Opens pull requests and commits from devin-ai-integration[bot]. Other bot accounts (for example autofix-ci[bot], a formatting bot) are neither agent nor human; merges from the base branch are neutral.

Cursor.notes: The pull request is opened by the developer's account but the commits are authored by cursoragent. A commit by any other non-bot account, other than a merge from the base branch, is a human commit. No Cursor ticket survives the 60-day rule.

Claude_Code.notes: Commits under the developer's account. The best marker (Co-authored-by: Claude or Generated with Claude Code) was in 20 of 50 sampled commits, under the 90% bar, so assessed at the merged level only.

OpenAI_Codex.notes: Commits under the developer's account with no marker in 50 sampled commits, so assessed at the merged level only.

checks: Does the ticket state what done looks like, as acceptance criteria, expected behaviour or a definition of the result?
Does the ticket give a reproduction, a failing case, an error message or a concrete example of the problem?
Is the change confined to named files, one module or one clearly bounded area of the code?
Does the ticket leave a design or product decision open that the implementer would have to make?
Does the work need an external system, credentials, a deployment, or a visual or UX judgement to complete?
Is this a multi-step change touching several parts of the codebase?
system_prompt: You are a careful software engineering classifier. Reply with only a JSON object and nothing else, in the form {"task_type": "<one of the task types>", "checks": {"acceptance": "yes|no", "reproduction": "yes|no", "scoped": "yes|no", "design_open": "yes|no", "external": "yes|no", "multi_step": "yes|no"}, "p_land": <integer 0-100>}, where p_land is your probability, in percent, that a coding agent's pull request for this ticket would be merged without a person having to rework it.

Read this ticket from a software repository and classify it.

Task types (choose one): {task_types}.

Answer each check with yes or no:
{checks}

Repository primary language: {language}. Repository size by stars: {stars_bucket}.
